claim: SpecVar integrates paired chromatin accessibility and gene expression data into context-specific regulatory network atlas and regulatory categories.
source: Here, we propose SpecVar to integrate paired chromatin accessibility and gene expression data into context-specific regulatory network atlas and regulatory categories, conduct heritability enrichment analysis with genome-wide association studies (GWAS) summary statistics, identify relevant tissues, and estimate relevance correlation to depict common genetic factors acting in the shared regulatory networks between traits.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a description of the method.

claim: SpecVar improves power upon existing approaches by associating SNPs with context-specific regulatory elements to assess heritability enrichments.
source: Our method improves power upon existing approaches by associating SNPs with context-specific regulatory elements to assess heritability enrichments and by explicitly prioritizing gene regulations underlying relevant tissues.
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the abstract describing the method's advantages.

claim: SpecVar can improve heritability enrichment, accurately detect relevant tissues, and reveal causal regulations as shown by ablation studies, independent data validation, and comparison experiments with existing methods on GWAS of six phenotypes.
source: Ablation studies, independent data validation, and comparison experiments with existing methods on GWAS of six phenotypes show that SpecVar can improve heritability enrichment, accurately detect relevant tissues, and reveal causal regulations.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a summary of experimental results.

claim: SpecVar correlates the relevance patterns for pairs of phenotypes and better reveals shared SNP-associated regulations of phenotypes than existing methods.
source: Furthermore, SpecVar correlates the relevance patterns for pairs of phenotypes and better reveals shared SNP-associated regulations of phenotypes than existing methods.
evidence: This is directly stated in the abstract as a finding from the study.

claim: Studying GWAS of 206 phenotypes in UK Biobank demonstrates that SpecVar leverages the context-specific regulatory network atlas to prioritize phenotypes' relevant tissues and shared heritability for biological and therapeutic insights.
source: Studying GWAS of 206 phenotypes in UK Biobank demonstrates that SpecVar leverages the context-specific regulatory network atlas to prioritize phenotypes' relevant tissues and shared heritability for biological and therapeutic insights.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a result from analyzing UK Biobank data.

claim: LD Score regression (LDSC) provides a widely appreciated method to estimate heritability and genetic correlation from GWAS summary statistics by quantifying the contribution of true polygenic signal considering linkage disequilibrium.
source: By quantifying the contribution of true polygenic signal considering linkage disequilibrium, LD Score regression (LDSC) provides a widely appreciated method to estimate heritability (Bulik-Sullivan et al., 2015b) and genetic correlation (Bulik-Sullivan et al., 2015a) from GWAS summary statistics.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to support the claim.

claim: SNPs contribute to phenotype through gene regulatory networks in certain cellular contexts, that is, causal tissues or cell types.
source: Another obstacle to genetic variant interpretation is that SNPs contribute to phenotype through gene regulatory networks in certain cellular contexts, that is, causal tissues or cell types.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as background knowledge.

claim: Stratified LDSC extends LDSC and can estimate the partitioned heritability enrichment in the functional categories.
source: Stratified LDSC extends LDSC and can estimate the partitioned heritability enrichment in the functional categories (Finucane et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation.

claim: The regulatory networks constructed by PECA2 model have been used to identify the master regulators in stem cell differentiation.
source: The inferred regulatory networks have been used to identify the master regulators in stem cell differentiation (Li et al., 2019) and interpret conserved regions for the nonmodel organisms (Xin et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation.

claim: Genetic variants in the regulatory network of cranial neural crest cells (CNCC) are elucidated on how they affect human facial morphology.
source: For example, genetic variants in the regulatory network of cranial neural crest cells (CNCC) are elucidated on how they affect human facial morphology (Feng et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation.

claim: Regulatory networks can help identify two kinds of relevant cell types to COVID19 severity.
source: Regulatory networks can help identify two kinds of relevant cell types to COVID19 severity (Feng et al., 2022b).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation.

claim: RSS-NET utilizes gene regulatory networks of multiple contexts and shows better tissue enrichment estimation by decomposing the total effect of an SNP through TF-TG regulations and HiChIP RE-TG regulations.
source: RSS-NET utilizes gene regulatory networks of multiple contexts and shows better tissue enrichment estimation by decomposing the total effect of an SNP through TF-TG regulations (Zhu et al., 2021) and HiChIP RE-TG regulations (Ma et al., 2022).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations.

claim: The phenotype-associated SNPs are revealed to be functional in a tissue- or cell-type-specific manner.
source: The phenotype-associated SNPs are revealed to be functional in a tissue- or cell-type-specific manner (Westra and Franke, 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation.

claim: SpecVar constructed regulatory networks of 77 human contexts that cover major cell types and germ layer lineages.
source: Specifically, we propose SpecVar to first leverage the publicly available paired expression and chromatin accessibility data in ENCODE and ROADMAP to systematically construct context-specific regulatory networks of 77 human contexts, which cover major cell types and germ layer lineages.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction describing the method.

claim: The M contexts included samples from all three germ layers, such as 'frontal cortex' (ectoderm), 'fetal thymus' (mesoderm), and 'body of pancreas' (endoderm).
source: The M contexts included samples from all three germ layers, such as 'frontal cortex' (ectoderm), 'fetal thymus' (mesoderm), and 'body of pancreas' (endoderm), which ensured the wide coverage and system-level enrichment (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to a figure.

claim: SpecVar obtained a heritability enrichment of 678.91 for LDL in the 'right lobe of liver', while ARE, SAP, AAP, and SEG gave heritability enrichment of 113.34, –42.09, 50.95, and 4.47, respectively.
source: For LDL, SpecVar obtained a heritability enrichment of 678.91 in the 'right lobe of liver', while ARE, SAP, AAP, and SEG gave heritability enrichment of 113.34, –42.09, 50.95, and 4.47, respectively.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with specific numerical values.

claim: SpecVar obtained the highest averaged heritability enrichment in brain tissues among these methods for educational attainment and cognitive performance.
source: For educational attainment and cognitive performance, they were relevant to brain tissues: 'frontal cortex', 'cerebellum', 'caudate nucleus', 'Ammon's horn', and 'putamen'. SpecVar obtained the highest averaged heritability enrichment in brain tissues among these methods (Figure 2—figure supplement 1a and b).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to a figure.

claim: Specificity can significantly improve the heritability enrichment.
source: We found that specificity could significantly improve the heritability enrichment. Among the five methods we compared, SpecVar and SAP are based on the specificity of ARE and AAP, respectively. SpecVar showed significantly higher heritability enrichment than ARE and SAP showed significantly higher heritability enrichment than AAP (Figure 2g).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to a figure.

claim: Chromatin accessibility contributed most to improve heritability enrichment for all six phenotypes.
source: We found that chromatin accessibility, which was part of the regulatory network, showed the highest effect in improving heritability enrichments for all six phenotypes.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on ablation analysis.

claim: Most genetic variants are located in the noncoding regulatory regions.
source: This is consistent with the fact that most genetic variants are located in the noncoding regulatory regions (Claussnitzer et al., 2015; Kumar et al., 2012; Smemo et al., 2014) and chromatin accessibility gives the direct functional evidence for genetic variants.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations.

claim: The specificity in SpecVar contributed at least four-fold improvement in heritability enrichment.
source: The specificity in SpecVar also contributed at least four-fold improvement in heritability enrichment (Figure 2—figure supplement 1e).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to a figure.

claim: SpecVar revealed that both LDL and total cholesterol were most relevant to the 'right lobe of liver'.
source: For two lipid phenotypes, SpecVar revealed that both LDL and total cholesterol were most relevant to the 'right lobe of liver' (Figure 3a and b, Table 1), which was consistent with the existing reports that the liver plays a central role in lipid metabolism, serving as the center for lipoprotein uptake, formation, and export to the circulation (Jha et al., 2018; Nguyen et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with references to figures, table, and citations.

claim: The liver plays a central role in lipid metabolism, serving as the center for lipoprotein uptake, formation, and export to the circulation.
source: For two lipid phenotypes, SpecVar revealed that both LDL and total cholesterol were most relevant to the 'right lobe of liver' (Figure 3a and b, Table 1), which was consistent with the existing reports that the liver plays a central role in lipid metabolism, serving as the center for lipoprotein uptake, formation, and export to the circulation (Jha et al., 2018; Nguyen et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations.

claim: SpecVar found that LDL and the total cholesterol were also significantly relevant to the 'fetal adrenal gland'.
source: SpecVar found that LDL and the total cholesterol were also significantly relevant to the 'fetal adrenal gland' and the adrenal cortex has been revealed to play an important role in lipid mentalism (Boyd et al., 1983).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation.

claim: The adrenal cortex has been revealed to play an important role in lipid metabolism.
source: SpecVar found that LDL and the total cholesterol were also significantly relevant to the 'fetal adrenal gland' and the adrenal cortex has been revealed to play an important role in lipid mentalism (Boyd et al., 1983).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation.

claim: SAP and SEG failed to prioritize liver tissue as the significant relevant tissue for LDL and total cholesterol.
source: However, SAP and SEG failed to prioritize liver tissue as the significant relevant tissue. For LDL, SAP identified the 'frontal cortex' to be the most relevant tissue. SEG identified the most relevant tissue to be 'HepG2', which was human hepatoma cell lines, but the relevance score was relatively lower (Figure 3a, Supplementary file 1c). For total cholesterol, SAP identified the 'fetal adrenal gland' and SEG obtained 'HepG2' as the most relevant tissues (Figure 3b, Supplementary file 1c).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with references to figures and supplementary files.

claim: SpecVar prioritized the 'frontal cortex' to be the most relevant tissue for both educational attainment and cognitive performance.
source: For two human intelligential phenotypes, SpecVar prioritized the 'frontal cortex' to be the most relevant tissue for both educational attainment and cognitive performance (Figure 3c and d, Table 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with references to figures and table.

claim: 'Frontal cortex' is the cerebral cortex covering the front part of the frontal lobe and is implicated in planning complex cognitive behavior, personality expression, decision-making, and moderating social behavior.
source: 'Frontal cortex' is the cerebral cortex covering the front part of the frontal lobe and is implicated in planning complex cognitive behavior, personality expression, decision-making, and moderating social behavior (Gabrieli et al., 1998; Yang and Raine, 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations.

claim: For both facial morphology and brain shape, SpecVar identified CNCC as the most relevant context.
source: For both facial morphology and brain shape, SpecVar identified CNCC as the most relevant context (Figure 3e and f, Table 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with references to figures and table.

claim: CNCC is a migratory cell population in early human craniofacial development that gives rise to the peripheral nervous system and many non-neural tissues such as smooth muscle cells, pigment cells of the skin, and craniofacial bones.
source: CNCC is a migratory cell population in early human craniofacial development that gives rise to the peripheral nervous system and many non-neural tissues such as smooth muscle cells, pigment cells of the skin, and craniofacial bones, which make it much more related to facial morphology and brain shape than the other 76 contexts (Cordero et al., 2011; Barlow et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations.

claim: Facial morphology and brain shape were revealed to share heritability in CNCC.
source: Facial morphology and brain shape were also revealed to share heritability in CNCC (Naqvi et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation.

claim: SAP and SEG failed to identify CNCC as the most relevant context for brain shape and facial morphology.
source: But the other two methods failed to identify CNCC as the most relevant context. For brain shape, SAP identified 'H1-hESC' and SEG identified 'tibial nerve' to be the most relevant tissue (Figure 3e, Supplementary file 1c). For facial morphology, SAP and SEG identified 'foreskin' and 'sigmoid colon' to be the most relevant tissues, respectively (Figure 3f, Supplementary file 1c).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with references to figures and supplementary file.

claim: POU3F3 is a well-known TF involved in the development of the central nervous system and is related to many neurodevelopmental disorders.
source: For example, POU3F3 is a well-known TF involved in the development of the central nervous system and is related to many neurodevelopmental disorders (Snijders Blok et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation.

claim: EMX2 is expressed in the developing cerebral cortex and is involved in the patterning of the rostral brain.
source: EMX2 is expressed in the developing cerebral cortex and is involved in the patterning of the rostral brain (Cecchi and Boncinelli, 2000).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation.

claim: FOXC2 is a member of the FOX family, which are modular competency factors for facial cartilage.
source: FOXC2 is a member of the FOX family, which are modular competency factors for facial cartilage (Xu et al., 2018), and its mutation is linked to the cleft palate (Bahuau et al., 2002).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations.

claim: FOXC2 mutation is linked to the cleft palate.
source: FOXC2 is a member of the FOX family, which are modular competency factors for facial cartilage (Xu et al., 2018), and its mutation is linked to the cleft palate (Bahuau et al., 2002).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation.

claim: By GWAS study, FOXC2 was previously found to be associated with brain shape by its nearest significant SNP '16:86714715'.
source: By GWAS study, FOXC2 was previously found to be associated with brain shape by its nearest significant SNP '16:86714715' (Naqvi et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation.

claim: SpecVar prioritized two SNPs ('16:87237097', '16:87236947') located in a CNCC-specific RE that may influence the expression of FOXC2 and the brain shape phenotypes.
source: Our CNCC-specific regulations further prioritized only two SNPs ('16:87237097', '16:87236947') located in this CNCC-specific RE, which may influence the expression of FOXC2 and the brain shape phenotypes.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the analysis results.

claim: The SNP-associated regulation of FOXC2 was supported by a HiChIP loop in brain tissues to link the SNP locus and FOXC2 promoter.
source: We checked the chromatin loops in the database of HiChIP (Zeng et al., 2022) and found that this SNP-associated regulation of FOXC2 was supported by a HiChIP loop in brain tissues to link this SNP locus and FOXC2 promoter.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation.

claim: For educational attainment, SpecVar revealed 7611 SNP-TG pairs in its SNP-associated regulatory network of 'frontal cortex', and 3693 SNPs (40.1%) of these SNP-TG pairs were also SNPs of eQTL in brain tissues.
source: For educational attainment, SpecVar revealed 7611 SNP-TG pairs in its SNP-associated regulatory network of 'frontal cortex', and we found that 3693 SNPs (40.1%) of these SNP-TG pairs were also SNPs of eQTL in brain tissues.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing validation results.

claim: For cognitive performance, there were 7494 SNP-TG pairs in its SNP-associated regulatory network of 'frontal cortex', and 3569 of them (47.6%) were also SNPs of eQTL in brain tissues.
source: For cognitive performance, there were 7494 SNP-TG pairs in its SNP-associated regulatory network of 'frontal cortex'. And 3569 of them (47.6%) were also SNPs of eQTL in brain tissues.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing validation results.

claim: SpecVar's relevance correlation showed the best performance in approximating phenotypic correlation (PCC = 0.522) for facial distances, which outperformed SAP (PCC = 0.467) and SEG (PCC = 0.405).
source: SpecVar's relevance correlation showed the best performance in approximating phenotypic correlation (Figure 5a and b, PCC = 0.522), which outperformed the other two methods: SAP PCC = 0.467 (Figure 5b) and SEG PCC = 0.405 (Figure 5b).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with specific numerical values and references to figures.

claim: For highly correlated phenotype pairs of facial distances, SpecVar performed best with PCC 0.467, which was the largest among SAP (PCC = 0.454) and SEG (PCC = 0.245).
source: By setting the threshold of phenotypic correlation to 0.4, we obtained the 363 highly correlated phenotype pairs of facial landmark distances and compared the three methods based on their performance on these 363 pairs of phenotypes. We found that SpecVar also performed best with PCC 0.467, which was the largest among the three methods: SAP PCC = 0.454 and SEG PCC = 0.245 (Figure 5c).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with specific numerical values and reference to a figure.

claim: For 206 phenotypes of UK Biobank, SpecVar performed best in the approximation of phenotypic correlation (PCC = 0.360), followed by SAP (PCC = 0.315) and SEG (PCC = 0.285).
source: First, SpecVar performed best in the approximation of phenotypic correlation (PCC = 0.360), followed by SAP (PCC = 0.315) and SEG (PCC = 0.285) (Figure 5d).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with specific numerical values and reference to a figure.

claim: For almost all the thresholds of heritability, SpecVar showed the best performance of PCC and mean square error.
source: For almost all the thresholds of heritability, SpecVar showed the best performance of PCC and mean square error (Figure 5f, Figure 5—figure supplement 2e).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with references to figures.

claim: SpecVar had the smallest variance regarded heritability among the three methods.
source: SpecVar also had the smallest variance regarded heritability among these three methods (Figure 5—figure supplement 2f and g).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with references to figures.

claim: 'Body mass index' and 'leg fat-free mass (right)' were correlated with a phenotypic correlation of 0.697.
source: For example, 'body mass index' and 'leg fat-free mass (right)' were correlated with a phenotypic correlation of 0.697.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing an example.

claim: SpecVar obtained a relevance correlation of 0.602 for 'body mass index' and 'leg fat-free mass (right)', while SAP obtained 0.342 and SEG gave 0.437.
source: SpecVar obtained a relevance correlation of 0.602, while SAP obtained a relevance correlation of 0.342 and SEG gave a relevance correlation of 0.437.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing an example.

claim: SpecVar revealed that 'body mass index' and 'leg fat-free mass (right)' were both most relevant to the 'frontal cortex'.
source: SpecVar further revealed that these two phenotypes were correlated because they were both most relevant to the 'frontal cortex' (Figure 6a).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to a figure.

claim: Body mass index has been reported to be related to frontal cortex development.
source: Body mass index has been reported to be related to frontal cortex development (Laurent et al., 2020) and relevant to the reduced and thin frontal cortex (Islam et al., 2018; Shaw et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations.

claim: Body mass index is relevant to the reduced and thin frontal cortex.
source: Body mass index has been reported to be related to frontal cortex development (Laurent et al., 2020) and relevant to the reduced and thin frontal cortex (Islam et al., 2018; Shaw et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations.

claim: Obesity and fat accumulation are revealed to be associated with the frontal cortex.
source: Obesity and fat accumulation are also revealed to be associated with the frontal cortex (Gluck et al., 2017; Kakoschke et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations.

claim: In the brain, SH2B1 enhances leptin signaling and leptin's antiobesity action, which is associated with the regulation of energy balance, body weight, and glucose metabolism.
source: For example, in the brain, SH2B1 enhances leptin signaling and leptin's antiobesity action, which is associated with the regulation of energy balance, body weight, and glucose metabolism (Rui, 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation.

claim: One common significant SNP '16:2896143' of 'body mass index' and 'leg fat-free mass (right)' was located in the specific REs of the 'frontal cortex' at the 90k downstream of SH2B1.
source: We found that one common significant SNP '16:2896143'of these two phenotypes was located in the specific REs of the 'frontal cortex' at the 90k downstream of SH2B1.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing an example.

claim: SpecVar revealed that the RE near SH2B1 regulated the expression of SH2B1, which was supported by a HiChIP loop in brain tissues to associate the SNP-associated RE and promoter of SH2B1.
source: Even though this RE was near the promoter of NFATC2IP, SpecVar revealed that it regulated the expression of SH2B1, which was supported by a HiChIP loop in brain tissues to associate the SNP-associated RE and promoter of SH2B1 (Figure 6c).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with reference to a figure.

claim: Integrating chromatin accessibility and gene expression data into context-specific regulatory networks can provide better regulatory categories for heritability enrichment.
source: The key message is that integrating chromatin accessibility and gene expression data into context-specific regulatory networks can provide better regulatory categories for heritability enrichment (Gazal et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with a citation.

claim: Extending the functional categories from noncontext-specific regions to context-specific regions can improve the heritability enrichment.
source: In addition, we show that extending the functional categories from noncontext-specific regions to context-specific regions can improve the heritability enrichment, which is consistent with other studies based on gene expression (Finucane et al., 2018) and ChIP-seq (van de Geijn et al., 2020) data.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citations.

claim: The annotation from chromatin accessibility contributed most to improve heritability enrichment.
source: We found that the annotation from chromatin accessibility contributed most to improve heritability enrichment (Figure 2—figure supplement 1e).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with reference to a figure.

claim: The regulatory networks of SpecVar, which integrated chromatin accessibility with gene expression data, played a more important role in improving heritability enrichment.
source: This meant that the regulatory networks of SpecVar, which integrated chromatin accessibility with gene expression data, played a more important role in improving heritability enrichment.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an interpretation of results.

claim: Specificity improved heritability enrichment by four-fold.
source: And specificity also improved heritability enrichment by four-fold.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section summarizing results.

claim: SpecVar defined the relevance score based on both heritability enrichment and p-value.
source: First, SpecVar defined the relevance score based on both heritability enrichment and p-value.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section describing the method.

claim: Using only heritability enrichment or p-value will not give a stable estimation of the relevance of phenotype to tissues due to the variability in the number of REs in the regulatory categories.
source: Because of the variability in the number of REs in the regulatory categories (Supplementary file 1f), using only heritability enrichment or p-value will not give a stable estimation of the relevance of phenotype to tissues.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with reference to supplementary file.

claim: SpecVar's regulatory categories had advantages over the existing functional categories to explain heritability.
source: Second, SpecVar's regulatory categories had advantages over the existing functional categories to explain heritability.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section summarizing advantages.

claim: With the constructed context-specific regulatory network atlas, SpecVar could interpret the relevant tissue by SNP-associated regulatory networks and interpret relevance correlation by common relevant tissues and shared SNP-associated regulations in relevant tissues.
source: Third, with the constructed context-specific regulatory network atlas, SpecVar could further interpret the relevant tissue by SNP-associated regulatory networks (Figure 4) and interpret relevance correlation by common relevant tissues and shared SNP-associated regulations in relevant tissues (Figure 6).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with references to figures.

claim: SpecVar performed better when the heritability of phenotype was low while LDSC-GC performed better when the heritability was high.
source: When using measured phenotype value correlation as the gold standard of phenotype correlation, we found that SpecVar performed better when the heritability of phenotype was low while LDSC-GC performed better when the heritability was high (Figure 5—figure supplement 4a and b).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with reference to figures.

claim: Relevance correlation and genetic correlation revealed the association of phenotypes in a complementary way.
source: These results showed that relevance correlation and genetic correlation revealed the association of phenotypes in a complementary way.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an interpretation of results.

claim: The usage of context-specific regulatory networks contributed most to the improvement of SpecVar.
source: The usage of context-specific regulatory networks contributed most to the improvement of SpecVar.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section summarizing findings.

claim: The context-specific regulatory networks can only cover part of the regulatory elements and genetic variants, which are highly essential and representative.
source: But the context-specific regulatory networks can only cover part of the regulatory elements and genetic variants, which are highly essential and representative.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a limitation.

claim: SpecVar is based on stratified LDSC, which may not perform well on admixed populations.
source: On the other hand, SpecVar is based on stratified LDSC, which may not perform well on admixed populations.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a limitation.

claim: Luo et al. have developed cov-LDSC to adjust the LDSC model to be suitable for admixed populations.
source: For example, Luo. et al. have developed cov-LDSC to adjust the LDSC model to be suitable for admixed populations (Luo et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with a citation.

claim: PECA2 calculated the trans-regulatory score by integrating multiple REs bound by a TF to regulate TG to quantify the regulatory strength of this TF on the TG.
source: One was the trans-regulatory score. Specifically, PECA2 hypothesized that TF regulated the downstream TG by binding at REs. The trans-regulatory score was calculated by integrating multiple REs bound by a TF to regulate TG to quantify the regulatory strength of this TF on the TG.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section describing the method.

claim: PECA2 considered a prior TF-TG correlation across external public data from ENCODE database.
source: And PECA2 also considered a prior TF-TG correlation across external public data from ENCODE database.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section describing the method.

claim: The output of PECA2 was a regulatory network with TFs, REs, and TGs as nodes and the regulations among them as edges.
source: The output of PECA2 was a regulatory network with TFs, REs, and TGs as nodes and the regulations among them as edges.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section describing the method.

claim: 77 contexts' regulatory networks were hierarchically clustered into 36 groups by trans-regulatory scores.
source: Firstly, we hierarchically clustered 77 contexts' regulatory networks into 36 groups by trans-regulatory scores (Supplementary file 1a).
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section describing the method.

claim: For a given context, a RE was defined as a context-specific RE if it was not overlapped with REs of other contexts.
source: Then for a given context, a RE was defined as a context-specific RE if it was not overlapped with REs of other contexts.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section describing the method.

claim: The context-specific regulatory network was formed by specific REs and their directly linked upstream TFs and downstream TGs.
source: Finally, the context-specific regulatory network was formed by specific REs and their directly linked upstream TFs and downstream TGs.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section describing the method.

claim: SpecVar used stratified LDSC to compute partitioned heritability enrichment.
source: SpecVar used stratified LDSC (Finucane et al., 2015) to compute partitioned heritability enrichment.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section with a citation.

claim: Stratified LDSC estimates standard error with a block jackknife and uses the standard error to calculate the p-value for the heritability enrichment.
source: Stratified LDSC estimates standard error with a block jackknife and uses the standard error to calculate the p-value pi for the heritability enrichment τi (Finucane et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section with a citation.

claim: SpecVar used R score ≥100 and FDR ≤0.01 as the threshold to pick up relevant tissues for a phenotype.
source: We used R score ≥100 and FDR ≤0.01 as the threshold to pick up relevant tissues for a phenotype.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section describing the method.

claim: The AAP method used all the chromatin-accessible peaks of each context to form a genome functional category.
source: The AAP method used all the chromatin-accessible peaks of each context to form a genome functional category, which was used for partitioned heritability enrichment analysis.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section describing alternative methods.

claim: The SAP method used the same rules of SpecVar to obtain specifically accessible peaks of each context.
source: The SAP method used the same rules of SpecVar above to obtain specifically accessible peaks of each context, and the context-specific peaks sets of M contexts formed functional categories of SAP.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section describing alternative methods.

claim: The SEG method was constructed by calculating t-statistics for differential expression of each gene in each context and selecting the top 10% genes ranked by t-statistic.
source: The SEG method was constructed by following the procedure in Finucane et al., 2018. First, the t-statistics for differential expression of each gene in each of the M contexts were calculated. Then for each context, the top 10% genes ranked by t-statistic were selected, and the 100 kb windows around those top 10% genes were used to form a functional category.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section with a citation.

claim: For the ARE method, all REs in the regulatory network of a context were used to form a functional category.
source: For the ARE method, we obtained all REs in the regulatory network of a context to be a functional category, and the RE sets of M contexts formed regulatory categories of ARE.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section describing alternative methods.

claim: The Spearman correlation of R score representations was used to define the relevance correlation for two phenotypes.
source: Then the Spearman correlation of their R score representation was used to define the relevance correlation
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section describing the method.

claim: SpecVar defined the association score (A score) to prioritize the REs by combining its regulatory strength and association significance with the phenotype.
source: We defined the association score (A score) to prioritize the REs by combining its regulatory strength and association significance with the phenotype (averaged -log(p-value) of SNPs located near the RE and downweighted by their LD scores and distances to this RE).
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and Materials and methods section.

claim: SpecVar extracted the REs with significant A scores (FDR≤0.05), as well as their directly linked upstream TFs, downstream TGs, and associated SNPs, to form the SNP-associated regulatory subnetwork.
source: We extracted the REs with significant A scores (FDR≤0.05), as well as their directly linked upstream TFs, downstream TGs, and associated SNPs, to form the SNP-associated regulatory subnetwork (Figure 1a, Materials and methods).
